answer.rationale: The two observed declines are activation (-6%) and onboarding completion (-4%). Onboarding friction plausibly drives both, since incomplete onboarding suppresses first meaningful action, so onboarding work is the highest-leverage single slot. I verify memory_86 (shortening onboarding) and memory_31 (signup field reduction) because they are the direct evidentiary basis for the intended action and both are older self-serve results that may not hold under a changed competitive environment; memory_86 is primary since it speaks to completion rates directly. I decline promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing: memory_73 explicitly records a material 30-day retention loss and an instruction not to generalize it, which conflicts with the sustainable long-term qualified revenue objective, and matching a price attack tends to buy exactly the churn-prone accounts that caused that retention drop. Referral incentive (memory_57) targets established customers and does not address the funnel stage that is degrading; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is a different segment from the one under pressure. Activation messaging (memory_91) is the runner-up and would be my fallback if verification shows memory_86's lift was small, confounded, or measured only on a cohort unlike the current one. Standard experiment scale rather than broad rollout: the inherited lifts are directionally credible but the quarter-over-quarter declines may have causes outside onboarding (traffic mix shifting toward price-shoppers who would churn regardless), so I want a clean read before committing further. Downstream value risk: removing signup fields or onboarding steps can raise completion while degrading lead qualification and data needed for routing and later enterprise motions, so the win condition must be activation and retained qualified revenue, not completion rate alone.
